- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid immediate peak overshoot.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If forecast drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to recover; add 1–2% upward bias in subsequent periods.
- Sentiment history with no significant change (all 0.00) suggests model should not overreact; use 10-day moving average as baseline.
